text: Every morning we prepare the cargo report. The figures are taken from the cargo system at zero eight hundred.
What is measured?
The volume of each tank, in cubic metres, and the temperature. And the boil-off.
Boil-off?
LNG is kept at minus one hundred and sixty degrees. A little gas boils off every day, and it's burnt in the engines.
Tank one, thirty-six thousand one hundred and eighty cubic metres. Tank two, thirty-six thousand two hundred and forty.
Good. Tank three?
On the report, thirty-two thousand six hundred and ten. But on the screen, thirty-six thousand two hundred and ten.
That's a big difference. Four thousand cubic metres can't disappear in one night.
Is it a discrepancy?
Yes. Let me check… The six and the two were swapped. A typing error.
Well spotted, Diego. The report is corrected and signed again. Figures are always checked twice.
Checked twice. Got it.
Show me tank three.
Where's the volume of tank one?
Where are the cubic metres?
Show me the temperature.
Where does the boil-off go?
Where's the discrepancy?
Diego, read me tank four.
And the temperature?
Is everything OK with the figures?
Cadet, how are the figures checked?
Tank two: thirty-six thousand two hundred and forty.
The report is sent to the company at nine hundred.
